It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates continued community interest and activity around Meta's latest large language model releases.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI components like transformers and Llama architectures.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its capability in conversational AI.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors for deployment.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced by using reinforcement learning.
The core mechanism involves using error information to dynamically adjust processor control algorithms.
This represents a significant step toward building stable and functional quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers he was hired to represent.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for betraying the victims.
The story highlights the severe risks and ethical compromises within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video understanding.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving perception and safety assessment.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Traditional LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes.
This metric allows for evaluation of quantized LLMs independent of absolute accuracy, crucial for resource-constrained deployment.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weights are universally critical across all LLMs.
Demonstrates that training these critical Super Weights in isolation actually causes severe accuracy degradation, suggesting limitations in current pruning/training methodologies.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive agents.
Addresses limitations in current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed, single-turn evaluation paradigms.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks involving LLMs and multimodal agents.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
The system addresses the constraints of single ReAct agents, which struggle to balance deep, complex research with wide coverage.
It aims to improve upon existing multi-agent systems by specifically enhancing recursive search depth and coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Overcomes limitations of existing refinement methods (like rule-based approaches) regarding quality and efficiency.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory despite sparse activation.
Introduces MAESTRO, a new method designed to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
MAESTRO overcomes limitations of existing pruning methods by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike heuristics designed for dense transformers.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the knowledge base and real-time capabilities of Claude Code.

stories.title: Apple’s failed self-driving car program left a legacy of powerful AI chips
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple's aborted self-driving car project is suggested to be a key driver behind the power of its current AI chips.
The project necessitated the development of powerful on-device AI processing capabilities.
The article explores the technological legacy of the unfinished automotive platform.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery demonstrated a new methodology for achieving reusability.
The development is viewed as an effort to emulate advancements made by SpaceX.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning, a temporal extension of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) for video.
Addresses the current limitation of existing video generators lacking specific supervision for CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to understand scientific lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on two key capabilities: scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final low-dimensional embedding.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this raw kNN graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond typical UMAP workflows.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the crucial distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge 3D pose estimation with biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low error in forward diffusion marginals guarantees numerical stability during sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with minimal forward-marginal error can still lead to a non-explosive, stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical stability during discrete sampling (reverse trajectory).

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new low-rank regularization technique for neural network compression.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as requiring SVDs or architectural modifications.
The proposed method is highlighted as being simple, stateless, and efficient during training.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper investigates the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, which is often ignored in standard workflows.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, before UMAP's projection distortion.
The research demonstrates that applying standard graph algorithms to this latent graph can significantly enhance data sensemaking capabilities.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The paper introduces ARDY, a new method for generating realistic 3D human motions.
ARDY aims to bridge the gap between high-control offline methods and fast, real-time online generation.
The research is highly relevant to fields like animation, simulation, and humanoid robotics.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: Addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
Introduces BioModule, a lightweight temporal transformer designed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The research is highly relevant to fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring language model reasoning capabilities to continuous control policies.
Proposes 'Latent Memory Palace' as a mechanism to organize information for better control reasoning.
Utilizes Autoregressive Variational Inference to enable flexible, deliberative decision-making in control tasks.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model, to address limitations in wildfire hazard assessment.
Addresses the challenge of conventional methods failing in vast, wildfire-prone landscapes.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to combine LiDAR and image-based data for better accuracy.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the crucial distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity in using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in large trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over extended periods.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper investigates the capability and bias of LLMs used as 'judges' or reward models in reinforcement learning for citation verification.
It addresses the critical need to calibrate LLMs used to assess the quality of source attribution in deep-research systems.
The study focuses on structured rubric tasks where search-grounded LLMs must support every claim with a cited source.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent draft token distributions.
Aims to accelerate LLM inference by improving the quality and structure of the tokens drafted before verification.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053 instances) to study communication variability.
Highlights a critical gap in current chatbot evaluation: reliance on simulated, articulate patients.
Introduces a new patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotion, and conversational strategy.

stories.title: [GCP Billing & Vertex AI] Solving Gemini Cost Allocation in a Single Project: Vertex AI Dynamic Billing Labels in Action
stories.author: evanlin
bullet_points: Addresses a common operational challenge: accurately allocating Gemini API costs within a single GCP project.
Highlights the practical use of Vertex AI Dynamic Billing Labels as a solution for cost management.
Relevant for MLOps engineers and cloud architects working with large-scale generative AI deployments on GCP.

stories.title: HACKHAZARDS'26
stories.author: rudrakshi_agarwal
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Dial2AI,' a system designed to make Generative AI accessible via a phone call.
Key feature emphasizes extreme accessibility, requiring no internet connection, smartphone, or dedicated app.
The concept addresses barriers to AI adoption by leveraging basic telephony infrastructure.
